summary: The locked fields correctly stay at zero/null this pass (0 wall-time, 0 experiments, 0 compute-bound tasks, no slowest-experiments, GPU-idle not evaluable) and the newly-raised TIMING INTEGRITY MISMATCH is, on inspection, very likely a false positive in the mismatch-detector itself rather than evidence of untracked experiment activity: git log since the prior retro commit (958859613) shows exactly one subsequent commit (a docs-sync task, not an experiment), and ops/changelog.md contains exactly one reference to '2026.07.475' -- the prior retro pass's own appended summary line.
bottlenecks_identified: TIMING DATA scope only: zero experiment commits exist to analyze this pass; the locked numeric fields are correctly zero/null and no slowest-experiment, duration, or DualGPURunner finding is supported by that block.

The TIMING INTEGRITY MISMATCH flag is very likely a self-referential false positive: scripts/research_conductor.py (read-only inspection, not modified) builds `milestone_marker = f"milestone {current}"` at the mismatch check but then tests `current in changelog_text` -- the bare milestone string, not `milestone_marker` -- so the check trivially fires the moment ANY text in changelog.md contains the milestone number, including this very task's own mandated changelog append from the prior pass. `milestone_marker` is dead code; the real check has no way to distinguish 'changelog shows real committed experiment work' from 'changelog shows a prior retro's own summary line'.

Because every retro pass is itself required to append a changelog line naming the milestone (this task's deliverable 2), any milestone that gets a second or later retro pass will ALWAYS trip retro_timing_integrity_mismatch=True regardless of whether real experiment activity occurred in between -- the detector poisons itself on its own output.

Supplementary (ops/conductor-log.md, outside the TIMING DATA block): no PHASE/experiment task attempts are logged between the 10:35 UTC success carried over from the prior pass and 11:43 UTC -- a roughly 68-minute gap containing only one entry, a 'Plan next milestone' attempt that failed via a 1201s Codex CLI idle timeout. This is the fourth such ~20-minute Codex planner timeout logged today alone (06:14, 07:05, 07:56, 11:43 UTC), matching the recurring long-prompt Codex-CLI stall pattern CLAUDE.md's Codex-Default-v2 section already documents from a prior milestone.
improvements_suggested: Fix the dead-variable bug: change the mismatch condition to actually test `milestone_marker in changelog_text` (or, better, restrict the scan to changelog entries authored after this retro's own `generated_at`) so a retro's own mandated changelog append can no longer retroactively poison the check meant to catch genuinely-missed experiment commits.

Until that fix lands, treat any retro_timing_integrity_mismatch=true flag on a milestone that has already had a prior retro pass as a probable self-trigger -- cross-check git log since the prior retro's commit and grep changelog.md for the milestone string before trusting the flag, as this pass did.

Investigate the recurring ~1201s Codex CLI 'Plan next milestone' idle-timeout (4 occurrences today) -- same signature as the known long-prompt Codex-CLI stall class; a shorter idle-timeout with chunked-prompt retry would avoid burning a full 20 minutes of silence per failed attempt.

When a milestone's task queue appears exhausted (here: 12 tasks queued at activation, several GATE_BLOCKed via cross-task retirement, one completed via artifact reuse, then a long silent gap before the next logged line), have the conductor log an explicit 'queue exhausted, moving to planning' marker so retro analysis doesn't have to infer 'stalled' vs 'working as intended' from a timestamp gap.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Patch the retro_timing_integrity_mismatch check (scripts/research_conductor.py, the mismatch block that builds but never uses `milestone_marker`) so it can no longer self-trigger on a retro's own previously-appended changelog line.
Diagnose the recurring 1201s 'Plan next milestone' Codex CLI idle-timeout (4x today) -- a repeat-offender pattern across multiple milestones, not a one-off.

Confirm whether milestone 2026.07.475's queue is genuinely exhausted (one reuse success, several cross-task GATE_BLOCKs, no further PHASE attempts logged since 10:35 UTC) and let 2026.07.476 activate rather than continuing to retry a stalled planner against an already-drained milestone.
meta_reflection: This pass is a small real-world instance of CLAUDE.md's 'the auditor now has an auditor' principle: the mismatch check exists specifically to catch a FALSE-ZERO detector gap (the .469/.472/.473/.474 saga), but on the first milestone where a prior retro pass had already left its own changelog line behind, the mismatch-detector itself produced what looks like a false alarm -- a reminder to verify any anomaly flag against independent evidence (git log, direct grep) before treating it as a genuine new finding, exactly as this pass did before writing up a conclusion.
